cards.subject: Half a zone
lines: At launch the Hinterlands had no Horde settlement at all. Horde players ran a level forty-to-fifty zone with no inn, no forge, no flight master and no graveyard anywhere near them.
Revantusk Village arrived in patch 1.5.0, with a new graveyard at the Overlook Cliffs — which tells you how the corpse runs had been going.

cards.subject: The Wildhammer are not Alliance
lines: They are independent — friendly to adventurers who earn it, and members of nothing.
The tell is that they have their own reputation bar.
They only pledge to the Alliance in Cataclysm, after Magni is turned to diamond.

cards.subject: One pass in
cards.tag: And it runs through a war
lines: There is a single mountain pass into the Hinterlands, out of Hillsbrad near Durnholde. Everything else is a flight path.
Alliance players walking in have to cross the Tarren Mill and Southshore corridor first.
That is a large part of why the zone got skipped.

cards.subject: Quel'Danil Lodge
cards.tag: The high elves you are sent to kill
lines: The Highvale elves keep the main high elf holding in all of Lordaeron here — diplomats, keeping records of births, deaths and seasons.
Their alliance with the Wildhammers is what makes them a target.
Horde players are sent to kill scholars and burn the archive.

cards.subject: Skulk Rock
cards.tag: A troll ruin full of oozes
lines: Its cave grows Ghost Mushroom, one of very few places above ground where the stuff turns up.
Ghost Mushroom was the road to invisibility potions, and every warlock's epic mount ate two Elixirs of Shadow Power.
This cave had an economy.

cards.subject: Agol'watha
cards.tag: A temple turned into a nursery
lines: It was a temple of the late Amani Empire. The Vilebranch took it and now use it to guard their spider eggs, with sludges through the rest.
The Eye of Shadra was kept in it.
This ruin and the spider altar across the zone are the same story.

cards.subject: You can call a loa out of the ground
lines: At the altar, players summon Shadra — Venom Queen, Mistress of Spies — by speaking her true name, Elortha no Shadra.
Then they harvest her venom for Forsaken apothecaries.
This game let you summon a Wild God years before it used the word loa out loud.

cards.subject: Gammerita
cards.tag: In the water off the cliffs
lines: A turtle four times the size of every other snapjaw on that coast, and blue where they are red.
Not a rare — she comes back in about two minutes.
She is very probably named after Gamera, and she stole an angler's best lure.

cards.subject: Seradane
cards.tag: One of four in the world
lines: A circular gateway into the Emerald Dream under a great tree, ringed by green dragonspawn.
Ysondre, corrupted by the Nightmare, comes out of this exact portal.
Added in patch 1.8.0, and most people in this zone never walk up to it.

cards.subject: Plaguemist Ravine
lines: A ravine with no mobs and no NPCs in the entire subzone — the only genuinely empty named place here.
The name is new in-world: plagued mist bleeding down from the Caer Darrow side.
Against a zone that is otherwise pointedly green and healthy.

cards.subject: Jintha'Alor
cards.tag: The second city of the forest trolls
lines: Built by the Amani Empire and named for an ancient Amani leader. Only Zul'Aman is bigger.
You are standing in the runner-up capital of a dead empire.
It is built exactly like a dungeon — tiers, a boss at the summit, a captive to rescue — and the game never put a door on it.

cards.subject: Elite from the base to the summit
lines: In here you climb a spiral city where everything on it is elite, with no instance portal at the top.
It was only made non-elite in patch 2.3.0, two years after this.
Anyone remembering it as soloable is remembering a different game.

cards.subject: The Altar of Zul
cards.tag: It rings a gong in Tanaris
lines: The altar crowning Jintha'Alor is where the Sacred Mallet becomes the Mallet of Zul'Farrak.
That mallet then summons Gahz'rilla, in a dungeon on the other continent.
The Hinterlands holds the key to a hydra in the desert.
